llm_proposer.assessment: The +3.2 dB receiver-power and estimated-OSNR steps, with unchanged BER and unchanged line-side OCMs, localize the event to the channel-specific drop path at S08 or to trx.och181.z telemetry. A decrease in effective WSS attenuation at S08 best matches the correlated increase, although the documented WSS fault describes attenuation increasing, so an unlisted adjustment or telemetry/calibration event remains significant; O3 is later and off the shared och181 path, so it is probably unrelated.

proposals.rationale: A channel-specific attenuation change in the S08 drop WSS after the incoming OCM can raise both received power and estimated OSNR for och181 while leaving other channels and line-side monitors unchanged. Against it, the documented mode specifically predicts attenuation drifting upward and power becoming low, opposite to the observed positive step.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A receiver-local calibration or gain defect could make trx.och181.z report correlated power and OSNR changes while external OCMs remain stable. However, documented RX degradation should produce receiver errors, whereas pre-FEC BER was unchanged and no alarm occurred.

A change in the S15 add-channel attenuation could alter och181 launch power without materially changing aggregate amplifier telemetry. It is disfavoured because downstream channel monitors, especially the incoming monitor at S08, should normally have observed the same power increase.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A change at the S15 transmitter could raise the received channel power and OSNR together. The documented fault primarily causes rising bias rather than a sudden 3.2 dB optical-power step, and downstream OCMs should have detected a real launch-power change.

proposals.rationale: Mechanical handling can cause an alarm-free power excursion. It is unlikely because the change appears step-like and persistent, and the S08 monitor on the incoming span saw no corresponding channel-power change.
